clue.text: Old court in which fighter is headed for trouble

definitions.meaning: the former Lord Chancellor's court of equity in England

definitions.text: in which fighter is headed for trouble
definitions.meaning: a boxer held in ... has his head locked under the opponent's arm, taking punishment

explanation.surface: A historic courtroom where some brawler is bound for strife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In chancery' is an old boxing phrase for a head trapped under an opponent's arm, so 'headed for trouble' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Court of Chancery was the historic equity court, and the same word names the boxer's trapped-head hold.

clue.text: Fresh sort of visitor

definitions.meaning: someone who calls at a house

explanation.surface: A new kind of guest has turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word for newly landed fish, and also simply one who pays a call.

clue.text: A scientific student of Jonson's play

definitions.meaning: an early experimenter seeking to turn base metal into gold
Ben Jonson's 1610 comedy about con men posing as gold-makers

explanation.surface: A science scholar studying a Jacobean playwright's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval experimenter in transmutation, and the title of Ben Jonson's comedy.

clue.text: Pines when one's gone and takes counsel

indicators.note: the numeral has gone, leaving the word without it

parts.note: pines are coniferous trees, conifers
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone yearns once a friend leaves, then seeks advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pines' looks like a verb of longing but is the plural noun for trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To consult or deliberate together is to take counsel.

clue.text: Climbers sometimes got up to the point

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to get up
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Mountaineers occasionally climbed to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbers' suggests mountaineers; it is plants trained up walls, and 'sometimes' covers that only some varieties climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling and climbing varieties of this flower grow up walls and trellises.

clue.text: Dutch house in Provence

definitions.meaning: the royal House of ...-Nassau of the Netherlands
a town in the Vaucluse in southern France, the principality the house was named from

explanation.surface: A Dutch home located in the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands' royal dynasty takes its name from a Provençal town of the same name.

clue.text: Redhead infuriates guides

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of red
angers means infuriates

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired person annoys the girls' leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' is one word but read as 'red head': the first letter of red. Rangers are the senior section of the Girl Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers form the senior branch of the Guide movement, so its members are older guides.

clue.text: Well known, but not Fleet Street top man

parts.note: ED, short for editor, the boss on a newspaper; Fleet Street was the home of London's press

explanation.surface: Famous, yet not a newspaper chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street is the London street long home to the national newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone noted is famous or celebrated.

clue.text: Audible nightly wandering?

parts.note: said aloud, nightly is knightly: the roaming of a knight in search of adventure

explanation.surface: Noisy sleepwalking after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audible' tells you to hear 'nightly' as 'knightly'; the answer is the wandering life of a knight errant.
explanation.definitionFit: The roving life of medieval knights seeking adventure is their errantry.

clue.text: Idolatrous poets ?

parts.note: idols are images, so worshippers of images would be image-ists, punning on a poetic movement

explanation.surface: Poets who worship false gods.
explanation.walkthrough: The early-20th-century movement of Pound and H.D. favoured clear images; the joke reads them as image-worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Imagist poets, led by Pound, prized precise images, which the clue jokingly turns into idol-worship.

clue.text: The animal in question must be seen to be believed

definitions.text: The animal in question must be seen to be believed

parts.words: The animal in question must be seen to be believed
parts.note: a creature whose very existence is doubted, so only a sighting would convince anyone

explanation.surface: A remarkable beast you have to witness for yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: The stock phrase 'must be seen to be believed' is taken literally: a creature many doubt exists in a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Scottish lake creature is disputed, so only an eyewitness sighting would prove it real.

clue.text: Looks round lease for loopholes

indicators.note: the first word goes round the second

parts.note: eyes as a verb means looks at
let is to lease out a property

explanation.surface: A tenant examines the contract for escape clauses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loopholes' suggests legal escape routes; here they are literal small holes for laces.
explanation.definitionFit: Small holes for threading cord or laces through are literally holes for loops.

clue.text: Awful rogue surrenders his love to Giovanni for reward

indicators.note: awful suggests the word rogue is mangled into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
Mozart's opera hero is Don Giovanni, so his title is DON

explanation.surface: A terrible scoundrel hands over his sweetheart to Mozart's seducer as payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surrenders' signals the loss of the O for love before the shuffle, and 'his ... to' are link words; Don is the title in Mozart's Don Giovanni.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerdon is an archaic literary word for a recompense or prize.

clue.text: Air-raids fail to hit round Temple Hill

indicators.note: the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: to miss is to fail to hit
Sion, or Zion, the hill in Jerusalem where the Temple stood

explanation.surface: Bombing sorties fail to strike near a holy hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Military missions are operational sorties such as bombing raids.

clue.text: Successfully defy dismissed Indian fighter

parts.note: out, as a batsman dismissed in cricket
a brave is a Native American warrior

explanation.surface: An expelled warrior from India stands up to authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' suggests India; it is the old term for a Native American, whose warrior is a brave.
explanation.definitionFit: To face down and overcome by greater courage is to beat in bravery.

clue.text: Such state is proper for a judge

definitions.text: Such state is proper for a judge

parts.words: Such state is proper for a judge
parts.note: alludes to the idiom about being as clear-headed as a judge

explanation.surface: This condition befits someone on the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'as sober as a judge' supplies the condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Judges are proverbially clear-headed and abstemious, as in the simile 'as sober as a judge'.

clue.text: So beset with difficulties, Wellsian hero grasps point

indicators.note: grasps means the name holds the point inside it

parts.note: Mr Britling, hero of H. G. Wells's novel Mr Britling Sees It Through
S, south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A Wells character, beset by trouble, takes hold of a sharp tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A task bristling with problems is thickly covered with them, like a hedgehog with spines.

clue.text: Jerked impatiently as dress was trimmed

definitions.meaning: flung oneself about or stormed off in a temper
had a decorative gathered frill sewn on as edging

explanation.surface: Someone stalked off in a huff while their gown was being hemmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Storming off with an angry jerk, and also edged with ruffled frills.

clue.text: Back start of retaliations, but not yet

indicators.note: back says the kept letters are read from the end
only the opening part of the word is kept, its ending dropped

explanation.surface: Supporting the beginning of reprisals, but holding off for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of' keeps RETAL, the first five letters of retaliations; 'Back' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens later is postponed, deferred rather than happening now.

clue.text: Has another look at criticisms

definitions.meaning: to look over again or reconsider
critical write-ups of books, plays or films

explanation.surface: Someone takes a second glance at the critics' complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for re-examining, and a noun for critics' published assessments.

clue.text: Island reads Times leader as madness

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: mania means madness

explanation.surface: An islander reads this newspaper's editorial and thinks it insane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' sounds like a newspaper's editorial; it is just the first letter of Times.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian state off the south coast of the mainland is an island.

clue.text: " What dire offence from causes springs" (Pope)

definitions.text: " What dire offence from causes springs" (Pope)

parts.words: What dire offence from causes springs
parts.note: the opening line of Pope's mock epic about a stolen lock of hair, with one adjective left out

explanation.surface: A line of Augustan verse quoted with a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rape of the Lock opens 'What dire offence from ___ causes springs': the missing word sits before 'causes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope's poem traces a feud to romantic, lovesick causes, the word missing from its opening line.

clue.text: Cases about tariffs

parts.note: C, circa, means about
rates are tariffs or charges

explanation.surface: Lawsuits concerning import duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' suggests court cases; it is packing boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Crates are wooden packing boxes, a kind of case.

clue.text: Expose deception of international body

parts.note: UN, the United Nations
a cover is a false front that deceives

explanation.surface: Reveal the trickery of a global organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncover something is to reveal or lay it bare.

clue.text: Note soon to be one included in chapter

parts.note: C is a musical note
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A remark that someone will shortly be written into a book section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chapter' suggests a book; it is the body of clergy of a cathedral, whose members include canons.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral's chapter is made up of clergy called canons.

clue.text: Fish to exclude from slimming diet

definitions.meaning: something that bloats, a food a dieter should avoid

explanation.surface: A seafood to leave off your weight-loss plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole smoked herring, and humorously something that swells you up.

clue.text: At the same time a soldier and statesman

parts.note: both means at once, at the same time

explanation.surface: One man simultaneously a fighter and a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis Botha was a Boer general and later the first Prime Minister of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Botha commanded Boer forces and then led South Africa as Prime Minister.

clue.text: He tries to protect the old, and studies outbreak of native riots

definitions.text: He tries to protect the old

parts.note: cons is an old verb for studies or learns

indicators.note: an outbreak breaks the words apart so their letters are scattered and regrouped

explanation.surface: He preserves the past and studies a flare-up of local unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cons' is an archaic verb meaning to study or learn by heart; 'outbreak of' is the anagram signal, its riot image matching the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who campaigns to preserve heritage or nature works to save what is old.

clue.text: European language with tribal affinities ?

definitions.meaning: like the Israelite tribe of Dan

explanation.surface: A Continental tongue linked to certain clans.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and the suffix '-ish' means 'like', so split the word reads as 'like the tribe of Dan'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scandinavian tongue of Denmark, and jokingly 'resembling Dan' the tribe.

clue.text: Do they spend lots of time going from room to room?

definitions.text: Do they spend lots of time going from room to room?

parts.words: Do they spend lots of time going from room to room?
parts.note: split as two words, the phrase means to while away a very long time; whole, corridors link rooms

explanation.surface: Do these people waste hours wandering between rooms?
explanation.walkthrough: Corridors take you from room to room; split, the word means to spend a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Corridors and hallways lead between rooms, and split the word means to spend ages.
